text: On the MultiRC testbed, we evaluated a weak-to-strong training variant that randomly drops a fraction of weak labels each epoch, with a label dropout rate of 0.1. Across 4 seeds, the method attained a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.53 with a standard error of 0.18. No baseline PGR was supplied for this run, so the measurement should be read as a standalone estimate rather than evidence of a gain over any comparison condition; we make no claim that label dropout improves on standard weak-label training. The standard error of 0.18 is substantial relative to the point estimate, and with only 4 seeds the spread across runs is poorly characterized, so the true PGR could plausibly lie well above or below 0.53. Replication with a larger seed count and a matched baseline arm would be needed before drawing any directional conclusion about the effect of per-epoch weak-label dropout.
